title: Agents That Write Their Own Tools at Runtime — Sandhya Subramani, AWS
talk_summary: Speaker demos Strands Agents 'meta tooling': an agent with editor, shell, and load-tool primitives writes Python tool files at runtime, loads them without restart, and can similarly generate subagents. She then argues for evals and guardrails—sandboxed code execution, constrained permissions, observability—before trusting self-modifying agents.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent gets three primitives: editor to write tool files, shell to inspect workspace, load_tool to import generated tools from a directory; system prompt supplies tool template/spec/rules and says check existence first.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need just three types of tools. The editor, the shell, and the load tool

takeaways.what_they_do: Same meta pattern writes subagent files from a template and invokes them; demo splits itinerary task into flight/activities/itinerary agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'm saying just break it into two to four sub agents

takeaways.technique: Multi-level trace evals for tool and agent use
takeaways.what_they_do: Evaluate session end-goal achievement, trace helpfulness/hallucination, correct tool and parameters, and inter-agent sequence/messages.
takeaways.evidence_quote: did it use the right tool to get to that answer or did it use the wrong tool?

takeaways.technique: Sandbox generated code execution, not just agent container
takeaways.what_they_do: Run agent-written code in a sandboxed execution environment so it cannot touch other code environments or write/delete wrong places.

takeaways.technique: Constrain permissions and tool surface for self-modifying agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Guardrails: constrain tools, permissions, who can ask, and observability before allowing agents to create/modify/delete.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We have to constrain the tools. We have to constrain permissions.

takeaways.technique: Bounded self-repair loop on tool errors
takeaways.what_they_do: When generated tool/agent errors, agent recognizes failure and patches same tool/agent, then retries; demo also shows it can update agent when requirements change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it recognizes that it's erroring and it says oh man I'm ering let me fix myself
